notes_markdown:
**Field fixes from a real holiday-culling session** against a live
Immich server, same day as 0.4.0 — all remote browsing:

- **Portrait photos from a server now develop and export the right way
  up.** Server previews arrive pre-rotated, but the original files —
  used for full zoom, RAW develop and export — don't; culler treated
  both the same, so portrait RAWs developed sideways and a
  compensating crop then baked wrong-way exports. Orientation is now
  tracked separately for the preview, the original, and the RAW member
  of a stack, so every path decodes upright.
- **Stacks appear while the library is still loading.** Server-side
  stacks used to snap into place only after the whole scan finished —
  on a big library that read as duplicate RAW+JPEG pairs for a minute.
  The stack relations are fetched once up front, so photos group
  correctly the moment they stream in.
- **Big remote libraries open newest-first and stay put.** The
  end-of-scan swap used to reverse the order out from under you (and
  leave the filmstrip showing stale thumbnails).
- **Re-exporting an edit (`J`) replaces your previous culler edit** on
  the server instead of piling up a new version each time — and the
  new render joins the albums the photo was already in, so albums keep
  showing it. A camera pair inside a server stack keeps its stack
  identity too: the re-render joins the *real* stack (edit + JPEG +
  RAW), never a partial one that would orphan the RAW.
- **If stack information can't be loaded** (a key without permission, a
  slow server), the scan now says so in the warning pill instead of
  silently showing everything unstacked.
- Fixed: the × that removes a saved source flickered away under the
  pointer and the click opened the source instead.
